# Frame time

<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask bench-ui` from crates/ui-egui/examples/frame_time.rs. Don't edit by hand. -->

> **Generated** for Cella 0.13.0 at `ceffa92` (2026-11-26). Machine: windows x86_64. Whole-window CPU time of one frame, rendered offscreen with no GPU.

`cargo xtask perf` prices operations per command; this prices **one frame**, which is what a person actually waits on while scrolling and typing. The window is 1440×900 pt over 1,000,000 rows × 6 columns, 30 frames a phase, after six warm-up frames. A phase's median is the number; the budget is the point at which the CPU cost of a frame would start dropping frames at 60 Hz on this class of machine — loose on purpose, because this measures the CPU half of a frame and not the GPU, the compositor or a real window's input latency.

| phase | what it does |
|---|---|
| `idle` | repaints with the document unchanged: the floor every frame pays |
| `page` | scrolls one screen a frame: a new band of rows laid out and painted every frame |
| `jump` | jumps 60,000 rows every frame: cold bands, a new used-range origin — the worst case a scrollbar drag creates |
| `key` | types a character into the selected cell: the frame that opens (or extends) the in-cell editor |
| `commit` | Enter with the editor open: the value is written and every formula reading it is recalculated — the workbook carries one `SUM` over the whole edited column, so this is the wait after typing into a cell a million-row report watches |
| `undo` | Ctrl+Z over one of those commits: the same restore, backwards |
| `drag` | the pointer dragged across the grid with the button down: the selection grows and the frame paints it |

The last four are the **interaction** half: a keystroke, a commit, an undo and a drag, each timed as the frame that shows it. `commit` and `undo` are the only phases whose number is mostly engine work (a recalculation), so their budgets are a guard against "the whole graph is rebuilt on every keystroke", not a frame budget.

| phase | median | min | p90 | max | budget | of budget |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `idle` | 1.0 ms | 828 us | 1.6 ms | 2.4 ms | 3.0 ms | 34% |
| `page` | 2.0 ms | 1.5 ms | 2.8 ms | 3.3 ms | 6.0 ms | 33% |
| `jump` | 1.7 ms | 1.4 ms | 2.5 ms | 2.7 ms | 8.0 ms | 22% |
| `key` | 1.1 ms | 929 us | 2.2 ms | 2.6 ms | 5.0 ms | 23% |
| `commit` | 15 ms | 14 ms | 16 ms | 18 ms | 250 ms | 6% |
| `undo` | 3.3 ms | 2.8 ms | 4.2 ms | 16 ms | 250 ms | 1% |
| `drag` | 1.2 ms | 978 us | 2.2 ms | 3.2 ms | 5.0 ms | 23% |

Every phase is within budget. What a regression looks like: a frame that reads the store per visible cell, a used-range walk per frame, or layout work that stopped being cached shows up in `page` and `jump` long before it shows up in any command's time.

## What a view setting costs per frame

A view setting is a state a frame paints, not a command that does work: setting it is free, and the cost is the repaint afterwards. Every command the coverage ledger marks `ui` is here. Each row turns its setting on in a session of its own holding a copy of the same workbook and times the same two frames the phases above time: `still` is a repaint with nothing moving, `scroll` scrolls one screen a frame. `(none)` is the same measurement with no setting changed.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| `(none)` | 984 us | 1.8 ms | 1.00× | no setting: the baseline |
| `formulas.showFormulas` | 1.0 ms | 1.7 ms | 0.96× | every cell shows its formula instead of its value |

No setting makes the scrolling frame more than 1.4 times the baseline: the frame cost of the sheet is where the data is, not how it is shown.

## What this does not measure

- **The GPU**: no wgpu here, so no present, no vsync, no texture upload. The repository owns the CPU half of a frame; the graphics driver owns the other one.
- **A real window**: input latency, the compositor and DPI changes are the desktop shell's, and `plan/bench/` has the scripts that measured them once (startup ~1.02 s, input-to-state ~40 ms round trip).
- **Other platforms**: one Windows machine.
